font_families.usage: The application's default typeface, set on <html>: all text no other role takes
Headings: Heading, the titles of Card, Dialog, Drawer and Sheet, the Logo
Code and tabular values: CodeBlock, the values of a Chart tooltip; always monospace
Kbd keys, the title of a CodeBlock, long editorial content; never for the interface

type_scale.usage: Text that stays 12px in every brand: badges, Kbd, Tooltip, menu shortcuts and group labels, chart legends, a caption
Text that stays 14px in every brand: a screen's own line that no component draws (a result count, a prompt under a form), inline code
Emphasized body text, introductions; Heading level 3
Hero text a screen draws; no component uses it
Display text a screen draws, rare; no component uses it

text_roles.usage: Component text: Button, Label, FieldLabel, menu items, TabsTrigger, table cells, FieldError
A surface's running text: Card, CardDescription, DialogDescription, FieldDescription
Titles inside a component: CardTitle, DialogTitle, the FieldLegend legend
The text typed in Input, Textarea and the Questionnaire input, always with md:text-ui beside it

font_weights.usage: Buttons, tabs, badges, component titles (CardTitle, DialogTitle…), table headers
Headings — Heading draws it at every level
Strong emphasis a screen draws; the Logo

letter_spacings.usage: Headings — Heading draws it at every level
Captions a screen draws; no component uses it
All-caps text, overlines; no component uses it
Keyboard shortcuts in menus and Command

usage_rules: **`font-body` is the default typeface, and the brand chooses it** — never override `font-family` on standard UI components without design approval.

**A heading is a `Heading`, a field label a `FieldLabel`** — each draws its own size, weight, tracking and line height, so pass it no `text-*`, `font-*`, `tracking-*` or `leading-*` class. For text a screen draws itself, a `text-*` class already carries its paired line height: add `leading-*` only to change it.
**`tracking-tight` belongs to headings** — `Heading` draws it at every level; on running text, negative spacing hurts readability.
**`tracking-wider` is for all-caps only** — never use it on regular lowercase text. `tracking-widest` is for keyboard shortcuts only.

**A strict weight hierarchy** — `normal` → body text, labels and descriptions, `medium` → buttons, tabs, badges and component titles, `semibold` → headings, `bold` → strong emphasis a screen draws. A field label stays `normal`.

**Next to components, text uses a role** — `text-ui`, `text-description` or `text-title`, the role of what it sits beside, so that it matches them in either brand. `text-xs` and `text-sm` are fixed sizes: use them only for text that must not follow the brand, and `text-sm` for a screen's own line that no component draws (a result count).
**`font-mono` means code** — write it on code and tabular values only, and write it even where the page already looks monospace.
**A text role in a `cn` call needs the `cn` of `@/lib/cn`** — the stock `cn` of `@/lib/utils` drops the role.
